solution:
The correct answer is __**option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Indus and Ravi**: The Ravi River is one of the five rivers of Punjab in northwestern India and eastern Pakistan. It is a significant tributary of the Indus River.
 
• **Yamuna and Hindon**: The Hindon River is a tributary of the Yamuna River in India, contributing to the Yamuna's flow.
 
• **Kali and Gori**: The Kali River, also known as the Sharda River, has a notable tributary called the Gori River.
 
• **Narmada and Dudhi**: The Dudhi River is a tributary of the Narmada River, which flows westwards across central India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indus River System**

 
 
• The Indus River is one of the longest rivers in the world, flowing through China, India, and Pakistan.
 
• Major tributaries include the Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej rivers.
 
• The river plays a crucial role in the agricultural economy of Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **Yamuna River**
 
 
• The Yamuna is the second-largest tributary river of the Ganges by discharge and the longest tributary in India.
 
• It flows through several states, including Uttarakhand, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Delhi.
 
• Major tributaries include the Tons, Chambal, Sindh, Betwa, and Ken rivers.
 
 
 
• **Kali River (Sharda River)**
 
 
• The Kali River flows through the Kumaon region of Uttarakhand, forming a natural border between India and Nepal.
 
• It is known as the Sharda River in the lower course and is vital for hydroelectric power generation and irrigation.
 
 
 
• **Narmada River**
 
 
• The Narmada is one of the major rivers in central India, flowing westwards over a distance of about 1,312 km.
 
• It is also known as the "Life Line of Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat" for its significant contribution to the state's water resources.
 
• Major tributaries include the Tawa, Hiran, Barna, and Dudhi rivers.
